baseline.name: LFU entries with linear eviction scan
baseline.approach: Track frequency/recency metadata per entry and scan all cached entries to choose an eviction.
baseline.time: O(c) eviction for c cached entries

archived.name: Direct key table and per-frequency recency lists
archived.time: O(1) get/put under fixed domains; O(K+F) initialization
archived.space: O(K+F+c+b), K=100005, F=200005 and b allocated lists

why: Minimum-frequency tracking identifies the eviction list, whose tail gives the least-recent entry among ties without scanning c items.
quantitative_comparison: Eviction changes from inspecting up to c entries to a bounded list-tail removal, but the archive reserves 300010 direct-table pointer slots and retains empty frequency lists. No timing improvement percentage is established.
tradeoffs: Fixed domains and substantial sparse-table memory may outweigh the lookup benefit. The destructor frees only the outer object, leaving allocated nodes/lists/sentinels unreleased; no complete-lifecycle quality advantage is claimed.
evidence_basis: Static eviction-work comparison with exact fixed-storage and cleanup limitations; no benchmark.
